content.Title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Valvular Heart Disease
Topics: Diagnosis of IE According to the Proposed Modified Duke Criteria
Use of TEE and TTE in diagnosing IE and assessing complications
Significance of valvular vegetation and imaging techniques
Potential complications like paravalvular extension and embolic events
Recommendations for repeat TTE and TEE in certain cases

Definite IE.Pathological Criteria: Microorganisms demonstrated by culture or histological examination of a vegetation, a vegetation that has embolized, or an intracardiac abscess specimen.
Definite IE.Pathological Lesions: Vegetation or intracardiac abscesses confirmed by histological examination showing active endocarditis.
Clinical Criteria: 1 major criterion and 3 minor criteria; or

Possible IE: 1 major criterion and 1 minor criterion; or
Rejected IE: Firm alternative diagnosis explaining evidence of IE; or
Resolution of IE syndrome with antibiotic therapy for < 4 days; or
No pathological evidence of IE at surgery or autopsy, with antibiotic therapy for < 4 days; or
Does not meet criteria for possible IE as listed above

TEE.Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis: Slightly lower sensitivity than native valve
Advantages: Visualization of vegetations and paravalvular complications
Anatomic visualization (valve perforation, abscesses, pericardial effusion)
Hemodynamic evaluation (valve regurgitation, fistulae, intracardiac thrombi)
Detection and quantitation of valve dysfunction
Evaluation of ventricular size and systolic function
TTE.Limitations: Should be used as an adjunct in patients with echocardiographic features of IE on TTE.

Recommendations: Repeat imaging for patients showing symptoms of complications
Consider vegetation size under therapy for assessing risk for new embolic events
Early surgery indications include heart failure, paravalvular extension, and embolic events
Repeat TEE recommended when suspicion of persistent infection remains
Routine follow-up echocardiography is limited if no clinical deterioration or new signs/symptoms are present
